useCases.title: Digitally Empowered with California’s Instant Identity Card (IIC)
useCases.summary:
The California Department of Motor Vehicles’ (DMV) Instant Identity Card (IIC) is a fast, verifiable identity (ID) issued to residents who urgently need proof of identity. It helps people who don’t have their physical driver’s license (DL) or ID card, or lack a mobile device.
Introduced by the DMV in March 2025, IIC provides a cryptographically signed, scannable paper verifiable credential that contains the resident’s photograph, demographic information, and a QR code linking to a verification service. Over 3.6 million IICs have been issued in this combined paper and digital format.
IIC addresses critical gaps faced by unhoused Californians, disaster survivors, and residents affected by emergencies, who frequently lose documents needed to access essential services. IIC lets DMV teams working at disaster recovery centers or outreach events for the unhoused issue immediate proof of identity onsite, reducing service access time from weeks to moments. 
IIC also supports corrections related reentry programs. Inmates waiting for physical ID cards can be issued an IIC to ensure they leave facilities with valid identity documentation, improving access to services and reducing recidivism.

useCases.userJourney:
The IIC includes a photograph, limited demographic details, and a QR code that contains a digitally signed photo and data, enabling quick in-person identity verification. It is available to California residents who already have a DL/ID on DMV record and need immediate proof of identity to access aid or services.
Holders can present their IIC to any entity that has a mobile/electronic device with a camera, such as a smart phone or tablet. The verifying party can access the DMV verifying website on their mobile/electronic device, or by scanning the QR code printed on the IIC. 
Verification uses NIST IAL3 equivalent identity flows due to superior form of identity protected with verifiable credential architecture enabled by cryptography and revocation lists, which reduces fraud during disaster situations and ensures only eligible individuals receive aid. Social service providers, housing authorities, and the Social Security Administration have aligned their workflows to accept IIC to significantly accelerate completion of housing and benefits applications, cutting processing times from several weeks to a day or two for unhoused residents.

useCases.title: The California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Wallet: Supporting Diverse Credentials and Protocols
useCases.summary:
The DMV Wallet, launched in 2023, is a secure user controlled digital tool designed to hold a wide range of documents issued by the DMV and other entities, such as driver’s licenses, vehicle titles, and Disabled Person Parking Placards (DPPPs) in verifiable digital form. By replacing paper and plastic documents with cryptographically signed credentials, the Wallet addresses inefficiencies in issuing and replacing physical records, which have been slow, vulnerable to theft, and susceptible to fraudulent duplication. These challenges are especially burdensome for unhoused Californians and disaster survivors, who often lose vital documents and need immediate proof of identity. The Wallet provides a stable home for these credentials.  
By supporting both W3C Verifiable Credentials and ISO mobile driver’s licenses (mDL), the Wallet ensures interoperability and long-term sustainability across digital credential ecosystems. 
Public reception has been extremely positive. The Wallet maintains an outstanding 4.8/5 star rating across more than 100,000 independent reviews, reflecting widespread trust, convenience, and satisfaction as the DMV continues expanding modern, secure digital services.

Hundreds of businesses which verify credentials from the wallet

useCases.userJourney:
A user begins by downloading the DMV Wallet and requesting a mobile Driver’s License (mDL) from the DMV, which verifies the identity using their physical driver’s license and, when done remotely, a liveness check. The individual can then use the Wallet’s add-on feature to add a growing library of credentials, such as TruAge, vehicle registration, DPPP, and others. 

The DMV Wallet has an embedded privacy preserving offline reader that allows entities to verify credentials without network access or tracking users, ensuring high trust interactions for both individuals and service providers. Security is further strengthened through face matching validation, ensuring only authorized individuals can access or present their digital credentials. 

When customers call DMV support lines from a number associated with their DMV Wallet, relevant DPPP information automatically appears on the representative’s screen, reducing call times and improving service accuracy. The digital DPPP enables individuals who forget their physical placards to use their phones to validate parking eligibility, which makes it easier to locate, reserve, and access disabled parking spaces at participating locations.
